# package node

```go
import "github.com/otfabric/go-canopen/node"
```

Package node is a complete CANopen device (CiA 301) built from an object dictionary: [New](#func-new) chooses the communication services from the objects the dictionary has, [Node.Start](#func-node-start) starts them and sends the boot-up message, and the NMT state machine enables and disables them.

	d, _ := od.Standard(od.Config{NodeID: 5, HeartbeatMs: 100, RPDOs: 4, TPDOs: 4})
	// add the application objects, map them into the PDOs...
	n, _ := node.New(bus, d)
	_ = n.Start()
	defer n.Close()

#### Services {#hdr-Services}

  - NMT slave: boot-up, the state machine and the resets. A reset node restores 0x2000..0x9FFF and 0x1000..0x1FFF, a reset communication 0x1000..0x1FFF, to their defaults (a pending node-ID, see [Node.SetNodeID](#func-node-setnodeid), applies first, so node-ID-relative COB-IDs follow it).
  - SDO server on 0x1200 (or the default COB-IDs).
  - Heartbeat producer (0x1017) and consumer (0x1016); node guarding responder with life guarding (0x100C, 0x100D).
  - EMCY producer (0x1014, 0x1015, error register 0x1001, error history 0x1003), available to the application as [Node.EMCY](#func-node-emcy).
  - SYNC consumer (0x1005), which drives the synchronous PDOs, and SYNC producer (with 0x1006 and 0x1019), which runs while 0x1005 bit 30 is set and a period (0x1006) is configured; the node's own SYNC drives its PDOs too.
  - TIME consumer and producer (0x1012 bits 31 and 30).
  - Every RPDO and TPDO whose communication and mapping objects exist, with the reconfiguration rules of CiA 301 installed (pdo.Protect).

The services follow writes of their objects while they run (an SDO write of 0x1017 changes the heartbeat period at once, for example).

#### NMT states {#hdr-NMT_states}

As CiA 301 table 79 requires: in Pre-operational the SDO server answers and the PDOs are disabled; in Operational both run; in Stopped only NMT and error control (heartbeat, node guarding) remain, the SDO server ignores requests, and EMCY, SYNC and TIME messages are not sent (they are counted in [Stats](#type-stats).Suppressed; an error raised while stopped is still recorded in 0x1001 and 0x1003).

#### Resets {#hdr-Resets}

After an NMT reset the services continue with the restored dictionary: they follow the restored values like any other change (PDO COB-IDs, heartbeat period...), the heartbeat producer and the guarding responder take the new node-ID, the heartbeat consumer restarts its supervision (each node supervised by 0x1016 waits for its first heartbeat again), and the SDO server is renewed on the COB-IDs of 0x1200 (its counters restart). The error state restarts as well: the active errors and the history are cleared without an emergency message (the boot-up message tells the network about the reset); errors whose cause persists must be raised again. The drive of [WithDrive](#func-withdrive) does so for a drive fault after the boot-up.

#### Errors {#hdr-Errors}

The node raises these emergencies on its own, each cleared (with the error reset message once no error remains) when its cause disappears:

  - 0x8130 heartbeat or life guarding loss, while any node supervised by 0x1016 or the life guarding is lost (MSEF byte 0: the node-ID, 0 for life guarding). The error behaviour object 0x1029 sub-index 1, when present, then selects the reaction: 0 Pre-operational (from Operational), 1 none, 2 Stopped. Without 0x1029 the state does not change. A resumption clears the error but does not restore the state: the NMT master decides that.
  - 0x8210 PDO length error, 0x8220 PDO length exceeded, 0x8250 RPDO timeout, reported by the RPDOs (MSEF bytes 0..1: the PDO number). Leaving Operational clears them, as the disabled RPDOs forget them.
  - 0x8240 unexpected SYNC length.
  - the drive's error codes with [WithDrive](#func-withdrive).

#### Store and restore {#hdr-Store_and_restore}

With [WithStore](#func-withstore) the node keeps its parameters (the sub-objects with access rw, see store.Parameter) in a store.Store: the saved values are loaded at New and after every NMT reset (after the defaults of the reset areas were restored: so a reset node yields the saved values of every area, a reset communication those of 0x1000..0x1FFF). Writing "save" to 0x1010 sub-index 1..4 saves a group (all, communication, application 0x6000..0x9FFF, manufacturer 0x2000..0x5FFF; [Node.SaveParameters](#func-node-saveparameters)), writing "load" to 0x1011 deletes it so that the defaults apply from the next reset ([Node.RestoreDefaults](#func-node-restoredefaults)). A wrong signature is refused with the abort "data cannot be transferred or stored" (CiA 301). store.AddObjects adds 0x1010, 0x1011 and the verify configuration 0x1020.

#### LSS {#hdr-LSS}

With [WithLSS](#func-withlss) the node is an LSS slave (CiA 305) addressed by its identity object 0x1018. A dictionary node-ID of 0xFF (lss.Unconfigured) starts it unconfigured: it stays in NMT Initialising and sends nothing until LSS gives it a node-ID, then boots. Configured node-IDs apply at the next reset communication (an unconfigured node resets on its own when the LSS master switches it back to waiting); with [WithStore](#func-withstore) the LSS "store configuration" persists the node-ID, which [New](#func-new) applies.

#### MPDO {#hdr-MPDO}

Every PDO whose mapping sub-index 00h is 0xFE (SAM) or 0xFF (DAM) is served by an mpdo.Producer (TPDO) or mpdo.Consumer (RPDO), created at New and whenever a mapping becomes an MPDO later; they run in Operational, report their emergencies (0x8230, 0x8210) like the RPDOs, and the object scanner and dispatcher lists are validated (mpdo.ProtectLists). [Node.MPDOProducer](#func-node-mpdoproducer) sends.

#### SYNC window {#hdr-SYNC_window}

Synchronous PDOs are bound to the synchronous window 0x1007, measured from the reception of each SYNC: TPDOs not sent within it and RPDOs received after it are discarded (and counted).

#### CANopen FD {#hdr-CANopen_FD}

With [WithFD](#func-withfd) the node is a CANopen FD device (CiA 1301): PDOs of up to 64 bytes, SYNC, EMCY (20 bytes), boot-up and heartbeat in CAN FD frames, and a USDO server (package usdo) in place of the SDO server. Node guarding is left out (CAN FD has no remote frames).

#### Program download {#hdr-Program_download}

With [WithProgram](#func-withprogram) the node serves the program download objects of CiA 302-3 (0x1F50 program data, 0x1F51 program control, 0x1F56 application software identification, 0x1F57 flash status) and leaves the flashing to a program.Handler; see package program.

[Node.Close](#func-node-close) closes every service, and the services remove the hooks and watchers they installed on the dictionary: a dictionary may be given to successive nodes (see [od.Dictionary.HookCount](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/otfabric/go-canopen/od#Dictionary.HookCount)).

Callbacks (the options' handlers) run on the goroutines of the services and must not block for long.

```go
const IndexErrorBehaviour uint16 = 0x1029
```

IndexErrorBehaviour is the error behaviour object (CiA 301 7.5.2.31): sub-index 1 selects the reaction to a communication error (heartbeat or life guarding loss): 0 enter Pre-operational (only from Operational), 1 no state change, 2 enter Stopped.

Node is a CANopen device built from an object dictionary: the NMT slave with its state machine and resets, the SDO server, heartbeat producer and consumer, node guarding, EMCY, SYNC, TIME and the PDOs of the dictionary, enabled and disabled as the NMT state requires. See the package documentation.

#### func New

```go
func New(bus canopen.Bus, d *od.Dictionary, opts ...Option) (*Node, error)
```

New returns a node for the dictionary d on bus. The node-ID is the dictionary's ([od.Dictionary.NodeID](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/otfabric/go-canopen/od#Dictionary.NodeID), 1..127). The services are chosen from the objects d has:

  - always: NMT slave, SDO server (0x1200, or the default COB-IDs), EMCY producer (0x1014/0x1015 and 0x1001/0x1003 when present)
  - 0x1017: heartbeat producer; 0x1016: heartbeat consumer
  - 0x100C and 0x100D: node guarding responder (life guarding)
  - 0x1005: SYNC consumer; with 0x1006 and 0x1019 also the SYNC producer (producing while bit 30 is set and the period is not 0)
  - 0x1012: TIME consumer and producer (following bits 31 and 30)
  - every TPDO and RPDO whose communication and mapping objects exist

The node does nothing on the bus until [Node.Start](#func-node-start).

### type Option

```go
type Option func(*config)
```

Option configures a [Node](#type-node).

#### func WithAutoStart

```go
func WithAutoStart() Option
```

WithAutoStart makes the node enter Operational on its own right after its boot-up (CiA 302 "NMT startup" of a self-starting device), and after every reset.

#### func WithDrive

```go
func WithDrive(cfg cia402.DriveConfig, period time.Duration) Option
```

WithDrive makes the node a CiA 402 drive: a [cia402.Drive](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/otfabric/go-canopen/cia402#Drive) is attached to the dictionary (its objects are added where missing) and simulated with a step every period while the node runs (0: the application calls [cia402.Drive.Step](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/otfabric/go-canopen/cia402#Drive.Step) itself). A fault of the drive is raised as an emergency (its error code, with the error register bits of its class and the device profile bit) and cleared when the drive's fault is reset; cfg.OnError, when set, is called as well. The drive's error code is 0x603F, kept by the drive.

#### func WithEMCYOptions

```go
func WithEMCYOptions(opts ...emcy.Option) Option
```

WithEMCYOptions passes options to the node's emergency producer after the node's own (for example emcy.WithFDInfo or emcy.WithFDLayout for CANopen FD, or emcy.WithHistory).

#### func WithFD

```go
func WithFD(brs bool) Option
```

WithFD makes the node a CANopen FD device (CiA 1301), with bit rate switching when brs is true: every service sends CAN FD frames — the PDOs (pdo.WithFD: up to 64 bytes, no remote frames), SYNC (syncobj.WithFD), EMCY (emcy.WithFD: the 20-byte CANopen FD emergency, logical device 0, CiA specification 301 and the system clock's time unless [WithEMCYOptions](#func-withemcyoptions) says otherwise), the NMT boot-up message and heartbeat (nmt.WithFD) — and accepts them. The SDO server is replaced by a USDO server (package usdo), as CiA 1301 replaces the SDO by the USDO: both answer on 580h + node-ID, so they cannot coexist. The USDO server follows the NMT state (enabled in Pre-operational and Operational) and the node-ID. Node guarding uses remote frames, which CAN FD does not have: the guarding responder is left out. MPDOs stay 8-byte classical frames (package mpdo).

#### func WithHeartbeatHandler

```go
func WithHeartbeatHandler(h func(nmt.HeartbeatEvent)) Option
```

WithHeartbeatHandler calls h with every event of the node's heartbeat consumer (0x1016): boot-ups, state changes, losses and resumptions of the nodes it hears. It runs on the consumer's goroutine.

#### func WithLSS

```go
func WithLSS(opts ...lss.SlaveOption) Option
```

WithLSS makes the node an LSS slave (CiA 305, package lss) with the LSS address of its identity object 0x1018 (New fails without it). The dictionary's node-ID may then be lss.Unconfigured (0xFF): the node starts unconfigured, stays in NMT Initialising without boot-up message, heartbeat, SDO or any other service until LSS gives it a node-ID, and then boots (reset communication with the new node-ID). The node wires the LSS services to itself:

  - configure node-ID sets the pending node-ID of the NMT slave ([Node.SetNodeID](#func-node-setnodeid)): it applies at the next reset communication or reset node; an unconfigured node resets on its own when the master switches it back to the waiting state (CiA 305 as CANopenNode does);
  - after every applied reset the LSS slave learns the active node-ID;
  - store configuration saves the pending node-ID (and bit timing) in the store of [WithStore](#func-withstore) (under the pseudo index 0x0000, outside every dictionary area, so parameter saves and restores keep it); New applies a stored node-ID instead of the dictionary's, so that it survives restarts ([Node.StoredLSS](#func-node-storedlss)). Without WithStore the node answers "store configuration not supported".

opts configure the LSS slave: the logger, the LSS state handler and the bit timing handlers (lss.WithBitTimingHandler, lss.WithActivateHandler), which belong to the application since only it can switch the bit rate of its CAN controller. The node-ID, reset and store handlers are the node's (options setting them are overridden).

#### func WithLogger

```go
func WithLogger(l *slog.Logger) Option
```

WithLogger logs the node's events, and those of its services, to l. The default logs nothing.

#### func WithProgram

```go
func WithProgram(cfg program.Config) Option
```

WithProgram makes the node a programmable device (CiA 302-3 program download): the program download objects 0x1F50, 0x1F51, 0x1F56 and 0x1F57 are added where missing and served by a [program.Device](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/otfabric/go-canopen/program#Device) whose Handler (cfg.Handler) does the flashing; see package program. The program control 0x1F51 accepts commands in Pre-operational only.

#### func WithSDOServerOptions

```go
func WithSDOServerOptions(opts ...sdo.ServerOption) Option
```

WithSDOServerOptions passes options (timeout, block size, maximum size...) to the node's SDO server. COB-ID options are ignored: the server always follows 0x1200.

#### func WithStateHandler

```go
func WithStateHandler(h func(nmt.StateChange)) Option
```

WithStateHandler calls h after every NMT state change of the node, once the node's services have been enabled or disabled for the new state. It runs on the goroutine that changed the state (usually the NMT slave's) and must not block for long; it must not call [Node.Reset](#func-node-reset).

#### func WithStore

```go
func WithStore(s store.Store) Option
```

WithStore keeps the node's parameters in s (CiA 301 store and restore, see package store): the saved values are loaded when the node is created (New fails when s cannot be read) and after every NMT reset (those of the areas the reset restores), and when the dictionary has 0x1010 and 0x1011 (store.AddObjects adds them) writes of "save" and "load" to them save the current values of a group of parameters and delete them ([Node.SaveParameters](#func-node-saveparameters), [Node.RestoreDefaults](#func-node-restoredefaults)). Reads of their sub-indices 1..4 return 1 (on command).

#### func WithTimeHandler

```go
func WithTimeHandler(h func(timestamp.Event)) Option
```

WithTimeHandler calls h with every TIME message the node consumes (0x1012 bit 31 set) while it is pre-operational or operational.

#### func WithTimePeriod

```go
func WithTimePeriod(d time.Duration) Option
```

WithTimePeriod makes the node's TIME producer send the time every period while 0x1012 bit 30 (produce) is set and the node is pre-operational or operational. The default sends only on [Node.SendTime](#func-node-sendtime).

#### func WithUSDOServerOptions

```go
func WithUSDOServerOptions(opts ...usdo.Option) Option
```

WithUSDOServerOptions passes options (timeout, sessions, groups, maximum size...) to the USDO server of [WithFD](#func-withfd). The node-ID option is ignored: the server follows the node's.

#### func WithoutHeartbeatConsumer

```go
func WithoutHeartbeatConsumer() Option
```

WithoutHeartbeatConsumer leaves out the heartbeat consumer even when the dictionary has 0x1016: for a device whose heartbeat consumption is done elsewhere, such as the CANopen manager of package master, which supervises the slaves of 0x1016 itself (and must not raise emergencies or change state when a slave is lost).

### type Stats

```go
type Stats struct {
	NodeID canopen.NodeID   `json:"nodeId"`
	State  canopen.NMTState `json:"state"`
	// Resets counts NMT resets (node and communication).
	Resets uint64 `json:"resets"`
	// Suppressed counts EMCY, SYNC and TIME messages not sent because
	// the node was not pre-operational or operational.
	Suppressed uint64 `json:"suppressed"`

	NMT               nmt.SlaveStats             `json:"nmt"`
	SDO               sdo.ServerStats            `json:"sdo"` // since the last reset (the server is renewed)
	Heartbeat         nmt.HeartbeatProducerStats `json:"heartbeat"`
	HeartbeatConsumer nmt.HeartbeatConsumerStats `json:"heartbeatConsumer"`
	Guard             nmt.GuardStats             `json:"guard"`
	EMCY              emcy.ProducerStats         `json:"emcy"`
	SYNC              syncobj.ConsumerStats      `json:"sync"`
	SYNCProducer      syncobj.ProducerStats      `json:"syncProducer"`
	TIME              timestamp.ConsumerStats    `json:"time"`
	TIMEProducer      timestamp.ProducerStats    `json:"timeProducer"`
	// TPDO and RPDO are keyed by PDO number.
	TPDO map[int]pdo.TPDOStats `json:"tpdo"`
	RPDO map[int]pdo.RPDOStats `json:"rpdo"`
	// MPDOProducer and MPDOConsumer are keyed by PDO number (TPDO and
	// RPDO respectively).
	MPDOProducer map[int]mpdo.ProducerStats `json:"mpdoProducer"`
	MPDOConsumer map[int]mpdo.ConsumerStats `json:"mpdoConsumer"`
	// LSS counts the LSS slave of WithLSS.
	LSS lss.SlaveStats `json:"lss"`
	// USDO counts the USDO server of WithFD (which replaces the SDO
	// server).
	USDO usdo.ServerStats `json:"usdo"`
}
```

Stats is a snapshot of the counters of a [Node](#type-node) and its services. Services the dictionary does not configure report zero counters.
